rationale: C08 plausibly supplied a concrete geographic-boundary template: it introduces an area through “following-described boundaries,” then traces the perimeter through a sequence of latitude-and-longitude points connected by “thence” clauses and closes at the starting point. The child adapts this same drafting machinery to define the Korean combat zone. C05 is nearly identical but earlier and less temporally proximate; C13 uses the same boundary-tracing structure but relies more heavily on landmarks and bearings.

shared_material.child_excerpt: within the following-described limits: From a point at Lat. 39° 30' N, Long. 122° 45' E southward to Lat. 33° N, Long. 122° 45' E; thence eastward ...; thence northeastward ...; thence northward ...; thence northwestward
shared_material.parent_excerpt: within each of the following-described boundaries; ... Beginning at Latitude 36° 00' 25" Longitude 84° 07' 05"; thence to Latitude ...; thence to Latitude ...; thence to Latitude ...
shared_material.explanation: Both delimit a legally significant geographic area by introducing described boundaries and tracing a polygon through successive latitude-longitude coordinates with repeated “thence” clauses.
